#ICMA Sept 28 2026

library(tidyverse)
head(billboard)
billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = wk1:wk76,
               names_to = "week",
               values_to = "rank") |> 
  head(10)
# piping the billboard dataset to pivot_longer. then telling pivot_longer the cols i want to pivot are cols between cols names wk1 and wk76 inclusive. then im giving the argument names_to. naming the cols to be called 'week'. then i want to values to be called 'rank'. then head provides us the first 10 rows.
billboard_long <- billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = wk1:wk76,
               names_to = 'week',
               values_to = "rank")
#saving our billboard data thats pivoted in long format into variable called 'billboard_long'
billboard |> 
  filter(track == "Baby Don't Cry (Keep...")
billboard_long_dropna <- billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = wk1:wk76,
               names_to = "week",
               values_to = "rank",
               values_drop_na = TRUE)
billboard_long_dropna |> 
  filter(track == "Baby Don't Cry (Keep..." & week == "wk8)
Error: Incomplete expression: billboard_long_dropna |> 
  filter(track == "Baby Don't Cry (Keep..." & week == "wk8)
billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = wk1:wk76,
               names_to = "week",
               names_prefix = "wk",
               values_to = "rank",
               values_drop_na = TRUE)
#prefix is ignored when values and columns are set
billboard |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("wk"),
               names_to = "week",
               names_prefix = "wk",
               values_to = "rank",
               values_drop_na = TRUE)

ICMA 10-8-2026

Slides 15 - 16 (Include the following in your ICMA file)

ICMA question: what’s the difference between these two code chunks? Are the outputs the same? Answer here: the difference is the first one has ‘mapping’ the second one doesnt. the output does the same thing.

mpg |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(y = hwy, x = displ, color = manufacturer)) + 
  geom_point()
mpg |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = hwy, x = displ, color = manufacturer)) + 
  geom_point()
#this runs the same thing just without 'mapping'

Slide 19 (Include the following in your ICMA file)

ICMA question: what are these warnings about and why should we worry about them? Answer: default you can only use 6 values. this is something to worry about because it warns you it might not be interpretable. meaning its not helpful.

mpg |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = hwy, x = displ, shape = manufacturer)) + 
  geom_point()

#when you replace 'shape' with fill or alpha it's not a good use

Slide 42 (Include in ICMA)

Change the color of the line to something other than the default blue

ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = class)) + 
  geom_smooth(color='black') # aes mapping variables to properties - map color to this variable (black) - it draws a line then associates is to black. so just say (color ='black')
